Let
$$S(m,n)=1+\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}\bigl(k^{n}+(k+1)^{n}\bigr)^{1/n},\qquad L(n)=\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{S(m,n)}{m^{2}}.$$

We compute the inner limit $L(n)$ for fixed $n\ge 1$, then let $n\to\infty$.

### Inner limit (fixed $n$, $m\to\infty$)

Set $T(m)=\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}a_k$ with $a_k=(k^n+(k+1)^n)^{1/n}$, so $S(m,n)=1+T(m)$. The leading "$1$" contributes $1/m^2\to 0$, hence it suffices to find $\lim_{m\to\infty}T(m)/m^2$.

Since $m^2\to\infty$ monotonically, apply the **Stolz–Cesàro theorem**:
$$\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{T(m)}{m^{2}}=\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{T(m+1)-T(m)}{(m+1)^{2}-m^{2}}=\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{a_m}{2m+1},$$
provided the right-hand limit exists.

Now
$$a_m=\bigl(m^{n}+(m+1)^{n}\bigr)^{1/n}=(m+1)\left(1+\left(\frac{m}{m+1}\right)^{\!n}\right)^{1/n}.$$
As $m\to\infty$, $\left(\frac{m}{m+1}\right)^n=\left(1-\frac{1}{m+1}\right)^n\to 1$, so by continuity
$$\left(1+\left(\frac{m}{m+1}\right)^{\!n}\right)^{1/n}\longrightarrow\,(1+1)^{1/n}=2^{1/n}.$$
Also $\frac{m+1}{2m+1}\to\frac12$. Therefore
$$\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{a_m}{2m+1}=2^{1/n}\cdot\frac12=\frac{2^{1/n}}{2}.$$

By Stolz–Cesàro,
$$L(n)=\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{S(m,n)}{m^{2}}=\frac{2^{1/n}}{2}=2^{\,1/n-1}.$$

*Sanity check ($n=1$):* $a_k=k+(k+1)=2k+1$, so $S(m,1)=1+\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}(2k+1)=m^{2}$, giving $L(1)=1=2^{1-1}/2\cdot 2=2^{0}=1$. ✓

### Outer limit ($n\to\infty$)

$$\lim_{n\to\infty}L(n)=\lim_{n\to\infty}2^{\,1/n-1}=2^{\,0-1}=2^{-1}=\frac12,$$
since $1/n\to 0$ and $2^x$ is continuous.

### Conclusion

$$\boxed{\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{1+\sqrt[n]{1^{n}+2^{n}}+\sqrt[n]{2^{n}+3^{n}}+\cdots+\sqrt[n]{(m-1)^{n}+m^{n}}}{m^{2}}=\frac12.}$$
